groups.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.
groups.noteTitle: The history and development of the bicycle

questions.text: Izzy believes the 'safety bicycle' is significant because it was

options.t: specifically made for children to use.
the first bicycle to be similar to modern bicycles.
designed to travel at higher speeds than previous models.

questions.text: What effect of bicycles on the 19th-century working classes does Max want to highlight?

options.t: how people spent their free time
the way people found romantic partners

questions.text: What will Max and Izzy stress about attitudes to bicycles in the 20th century?

options.t: The popularity of cars reduced the status of bicycles in the 1950s.
New designs led to an increase in sales of bicycles in the 1960s.
An interest in fitness promoted demand for bicycles in the 1980s.

questions.text: What does Max say about a scheme to provide free bikes to school pupils?

options.t: He wants to see more evidence of its benefits.
He thinks it could cost the government a lot of money.
He questions whether all parents would support it.

groups.instruction: Which reason did each of the following people give for using a bike? Choose SIX answers from the box and write the correct letter, A-H, next to questions 25-30.

bank.t: Cycling is a convenient way to travel.
Riding a bike can be a social activity.
Bikes are a cheap form of transport.
Cycling is a way to spend time outdoors.
Riding a bike is good for mental health.
Riding a bike is good exercise.
Cycling can be done by all ages.
